description: Found while costing fz-sc8.14. On fz2 ad21e1635 (AOT build), String.length of a binary built by tail-recursive append ('ab' repeated) takes 0.15 s at 100 KB, 0.49 s at 200 KB and 1.63 s at 400 KB: about 3.3x per doubling, i.e. quadratic. Building the string with acc <> "ab" in a tail loop scales the same way (0.12, 0.40, 1.38 s). Elixir does both in milliseconds. Hypothesis, not yet confirmed: a binary match's rest (<<_::binary-size(n), rest::binary>>, as in String.drop_bytes) and a <> append each copy the bytes, where BEAM makes a sub-binary view and appends in place. Every grapheme or codepoint walker in lib/string.fz (length, graphemes, split, trim, slice, pad) pays this per step. First step: profile one walk to confirm which operation copies, then make it a view by construction on all three paths, with a scaling test that observes it (bytes copied per walk via telemetry, if the runtime can report it). Repro programs in the coordinator's scratchpad (l50000.fz etc.).
title: Walking or building a binary costs time linear in its length
